components.name: Telematics unit
components.description: The car's connection to the outside world.

threats.title: Attacker takes control remotely over the cellular connection
threats.explanation: The telematics unit is always online. If it has an open service or an unpatched bug, an attacker anywhere in the world could break in and use it as a doorway to the rest of the car.
mitigations: Close every network port and service that isn't strictly needed
Separate the telematics unit from safety-critical systems with a gateway firewall
Keep the unit's software patched through secure updates

threats.title: Fake server sends commands to the car
threats.explanation: An attacker pretends to be the manufacturer's back-end server and sends commands such as 'unlock doors' or 'start engine'. If the car doesn't check who it is talking to, it will obey.
mitigations: Use mutual authentication with certificates so both sides prove who they are
Digitally sign every command and reject anything with an invalid signature

threats.title: Vehicle data is intercepted in transit
threats.explanation: Location, driving behaviour and personal data travel between the car and the cloud. Without encryption, anyone listening on the network can read or copy it.
mitigations: Encrypt all traffic with up-to-date TLS
Only send the data that is actually needed

threats.title: Hacked back-end server is used to attack the whole fleet
threats.explanation: If the manufacturer's server is compromised, the attacker doesn't need to hack cars one by one. They can send malicious instructions to thousands of vehicles at once.
mitigations: Harden servers and restrict admin access with strong authentication
Monitor servers and fleet traffic for unusual behaviour
Limit which commands the server is allowed to send to cars

threats.title: Connection is flooded or jammed
threats.explanation: An attacker floods the unit with traffic or jams the cellular signal, so remote services like emergency calls or remote lock stop working.
mitigations: Rate-limit incoming connections and drop malformed traffic
Design the car so safety functions keep working when the connection is lost

components.name: OTA update module
components.description: How the car receives software updates.

threats.title: Tampered software update is installed
threats.explanation: An attacker modifies an update package to include malicious code. If the car installs it without checking, the attacker's code runs inside the vehicle.
mitigations: Verify the digital signature of every update before installing it
Use secure boot so only signed software can run

threats.title: Car is rolled back to an old, vulnerable version
threats.explanation: An attacker installs an older but genuinely signed version of the software that has known security holes, then exploits those holes.
mitigations: Use anti-rollback version counters so older versions are rejected
Revoke signatures of versions with known serious vulnerabilities

threats.title: Interrupted update leaves the car unusable
threats.explanation: Power loss or a dropped connection halfway through an update can leave a control unit with broken software, so the car may not start or may behave unpredictably.
mitigations: Keep a backup copy of the working software and roll back automatically on failure
Check battery level and that the car is parked safely before starting
Tell the driver before and after the update what is happening

threats.title: Update server is compromised and pushes malicious updates
threats.explanation: If an attacker gets into the system that builds or distributes updates, they could ship malicious software that looks completely legitimate to every car.
mitigations: Keep signing keys in a hardware security module, never on ordinary servers
Require approval from more than one person to release an update

threats.title: Driver is tricked into installing a fake update
threats.explanation: A phishing message or fake USB stick convinces the owner to 'update' their car with malicious software.
mitigations: Only accept updates through the official, authenticated update channel
Show clear in-car messages about where genuine updates come from

components.name: Keyless entry
components.description: How the car recognises its key.

threats.title: Relay attack unlocks and starts the car
threats.explanation: Two thieves use radio devices to relay the signal from a key inside the house to the car on the driveway. The car thinks the key is nearby and unlocks.
mitigations: Use ultra-wideband distance measurement to confirm the key is really close
Put the key fob to sleep when it hasn't moved for a while

threats.title: Captured key signal is replayed later
threats.explanation: An attacker records the signal when the owner presses the unlock button, then plays it back later to open the car.
mitigations: Use rolling codes or challenge-response so each signal only works once

threats.title: Jamming stops the car from locking
threats.explanation: An attacker blocks the lock signal. The owner walks away thinking the car is locked, and the thief simply opens the door.
mitigations: Give clear lock confirmation with lights, a sound or a phone notification
Detect jamming and alert the owner

threats.title: New key is programmed through the diagnostic port
threats.explanation: A thief breaks into the car, plugs a device into the diagnostic port and programs a blank key, then drives away.
mitigations: Require authenticated dealer access to program new keys
Notify the owner whenever a new key is added

threats.title: Weak encryption in the key is cracked
threats.explanation: If the key uses old or weak cryptography, attackers can work out its secret and create a working copy.
mitigations: Use modern, well-reviewed cryptography such as AES-128 or stronger
Give every vehicle and key its own unique secret
